title: DESIGN, PRODUCTIVITY AND WELL BEING: What are the Links?

findings.antecedent: new, green building (Miller SQA) compared to old industrial building
findings.mechanism: Green building features (daylight, views, air quality) are hypothesized to contribute to well-being.
findings.quote: The data show that the new, green building was associated overall with higher quality of work life than the old building

findings.antecedent: new, green building (Miller SQA) compared to old industrial building
findings.mechanism: Green building features (daylight, views, air quality) are hypothesized to contribute to well-being and performance.
findings.quote: and that it had a more positive impact on perceived work performance and job satisfaction.

findings.antecedent: new, green building (Miller SQA) compared to old industrial building
findings.mechanism: Green building features (daylight, views, air quality) are hypothesized to contribute to well-being and job satisfaction.
findings.quote: and that it had a more positive impact on perceived work performance and job satisfaction.

findings.antecedent: new, green building (Miller SQA) compared to old industrial building
findings.mechanism: Improved environmental conditions in the green building are perceived as healthier.
findings.quote: The new building was also perceived as “healthier” than the old building

findings.antecedent: new, green building (Miller SQA) compared to old industrial building
findings.mechanism: Despite perceived health benefits, general illness symptoms did not significantly change.
findings.quote: however, there were few differences in self-reported illness symptoms (such as headaches and fatigue).

findings.antecedent: new, green building (Miller SQA) for office workers
findings.mechanism: Improved lighting (daylight) and air quality in the new building for office workers likely reduced discomfort.
findings.quote: The exception was a decrease in headaches for office workers in the new building. Whereas 16% said they had headaches often or always in the old building, only 7% did in the new building.

findings.antecedent: new, green building (Miller SQA) for manufacturing workers
findings.mechanism: Manufacturing areas had issues with low air movement and potentially blocked views, negating health benefits seen in office areas.
findings.quote: There were no differences in the health and data reported for the manufacturing workers.

findings.antecedent: windows and lighting features in the new, green building (Miller SQA)
findings.mechanism: Presence of extensive interior and exterior views and high daylight levels contributed to very high ratings.
findings.quote: The windows and lighting received very high ratings by workers, particularly the presence of extensive interior and exterior views and the high daylight levels.

findings.antecedent: air quality in the new, green building (Miller SQA)
findings.mechanism: Green building design prioritizes improved indoor air quality.
findings.quote: Air quality in the new building was also rated more favorably

findings.antecedent: new building (Miller SQA) for night shift workers
findings.consequent: outcomes on all dimensions (quality of work life, performance, job satisfaction, health)
findings.mechanism: Lack of naturalistic amenities (outdoor views, daylight) for night shift workers meant benefits did not accrue, leading to more negative responses.
findings.quote: The data in the night shift had more negative outcomes on all of these dimensions; in fact, their responses in the new building were even more negative than they were in the old building (Heerwagen, 1998).

findings.antecedent: office workers compared to manufacturing workers in the new building (Miller SQA)
findings.consequent: positive outcomes on almost all dimensions
findings.mechanism: Office workers had better access to aesthetic and naturalistic features (daylight, windows, contact with nature/wildlife) compared to manufacturing workers.
findings.quote: Comparisons of the manufacturing and office workers show that office workers had more positive outcomes on almost all dimensions.

findings.antecedent: aesthetic and naturalistic features of the environment (daylight, windows, contact with nature, contact with wildlife) for office workers compared to manufacturing workers in the new building (Miller SQA)
findings.mechanism: Office spaces had extensive window views, interior plants, and decor, while manufacturing areas had blocked views and lower daylight.
findings.quote: Office workers rated the aesthetic and naturalistic features of the environment (daylight, windows, contact with nature, contact with wildlife) more favorably than did the manufacturing workers suggesting greater perceptual experience

findings.antecedent: office workers compared to manufacturing workers in the new building (Miller SQA)
findings.mechanism: Better environmental conditions for office workers likely contributed to more positive work attitudes.
findings.quote: Office workers also had more positive work attitudes, and were more likely to be in good spirits at work.

findings.antecedent: office workers compared to manufacturing workers in the new building (Miller SQA)
findings.consequent: likelihood of being in good spirits at work
findings.mechanism: Better environmental conditions for office workers likely contributed to better moods.
findings.quote: Office workers also had more positive work attitudes, and were more likely to be in good spirits at work.

findings.antecedent: move to the new building (Miller SQA)
findings.consequent: increased fatigue and feelings of being “overworked”
findings.mechanism: Likely due to a large increase in sales and manufacturing capability, indicating increased workload rather than building design.
findings.quote: However, both manufacturing and office workers reported increased fatigue in the new building and increased feelings of being “overworked.” This is very likely due to the large increase in sales associated with increased manufacturing capability.

findings.antecedent: new building (Miller SQA) compared to old building
findings.consequent: organizational performance on TQM measures (effectiveness, efficiency, quality, total productivity)
findings.mechanism: Modest increases in performance, though not statistically significant, were observed, potentially linked to improved worker well-being and attitudes.
findings.quote: For four of the TQM measures (effectiveness, efficiency, quality, and total productivity), there were increases in performance for at least five of the eight matched months. There were also modest increases of 0.5 to 2% on these four measures. Although they were not statistically significant, they may be very organizationally significant

stimuli.description: Comparison of an 'old building' (smaller industrial type, high ribbon windows, limited daylight, employee lounge, small outdoor seating, conference rooms, no exercise facility) with a 'new, green building' (Miller SQA: 290,000 sq ft, manufacturing plant, warehouse, headquarters, large-scale daylighting, energy efficient fluorescent lamps, daylight controls, energy efficient glazing, motion sensors, state-of-the-art HVAC, environmentally sensitive materials, minimally invasive site utilization including wetlands and natural field vegetation, enhanced IAQ, extensive recycling, local materials, lunchroom, rest areas, fitness center, basketball court).

limitations: Potential 'halo effect' associated with being in a new building.
Confounding factors not directly related to green design (e.g., color, aesthetics, spatial arrangements, new furniture).
Changes in organizational policies (e.g., decrease in employee profit share) as a confounding factor.
Inability to definitively determine reasons for negative responses from non-daytime manufacturing workers (e.g., working outside normal daytime hours or viewing the new building as a cost).
TQM measures showed modest increases but were not statistically significant.
Turnover rate was too low for analysis.
Absenteeism data was not collected in a way that allowed separation of illness from other reasons for absence.
